bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM hallucination rates and accuracy across different United States judicial jurisdictions, noting degraded performance in central country circuits compared to coastal ones.

Qualitatively assessing how LLM definitions fail to capture the offline speech of underrepresented minorities and rural populations without internet access, leading to a lack of regionalized meanings.
Observing the phenomenon where models agree with user-introduced misconceptions or non-factual legal premises (General Cognitive Error) in prompts to seek human approval.
Evaluating model performance and hallucination rates based on the year of the legal case, noting better performance on older cases compared to very recent or very old ones.
Measuring the negative correlation between the prominence of a legal case and the frequency of model hallucinations.
